correctness.rationale: Published Theorems 13 and 14 give exactly the two run-length transforms. Their common recurrence modulo two yields s(j+5)=s(j), with seeds 11110 and 10010, so all run-length restrictions hold at every index. Unique binary-word decomposition gives the two rational counting series, and the degree-one term plus a positive simple real pole forces exact Perron asymptotics and arbitrary-cutoff Theta exponents. The supplied checker reconstructs original binomial sums for 1024 inputs per transform and independently enumerates all binary words up to 14 digits; finite data are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Rampersad--Wiebe (2023) proves the two run-length transform identifications but does not count their odd-value supports. The 2016 Wu precursor treats different transforms. OEIS A124312 already gives the first companion count, which is explicitly treated only as a pre-existing comparator, not a new enumeration. The second transform's exact binary-residue support, rational dyadic count, algebraic entropy exponent and the exponential relative thinning against the first are not asserted by the inspected works. Focused semantic, formula, database and literature searches found no dominating statement, subject to possible unindexed equivalents.
residual_risks: One dyadic count (the first companion) is already recorded in OEIS A124312 and must not be counted as new independently.
An alternative-indexed automatic-sequence or constrained-binary-word count might imply the second series without an obvious name or matching keyword.
Automatic-sequence and regular-language techniques are classical; the novelty lies in their explicit new arithmetic consequence, not a general method.
Independent scientific review has not been performed.

value.rationale: The paper introduced this particular pair precisely because their fourth-order recurrence is identical but the seeds differ. Their odd-value sets have exact nested structure, sharply different algebraic exponential growth (about 1.966 versus 1.497 per binary digit), distinct optimal power-law exponents, and an explicit exponential relative thinning law. These natural arithmetic sparsity invariants were not supplied by the 2023 identities, and the comparison is not a restatement of the old OEIS first companion table. The result is intentionally narrow, complete and quantitatively sharp rather than a general algorithm.
